Rules of the RadianceHy4Flash repository.

## no-merge-without-a-measurement
A change of this repository is merged only when it was measured on a lane, and what counts is the item's own merge bar (`notes/backlog/CARDS.md`, section 2): the stamps or kbench rows it names and, where it asks for one, a served A/B before and after on one lane. Before you merge a change, read its review (`"$MOEBIUS" card <id> --json`, the `review` field, or the card's runs). Refuse to merge it - `"$MOEBIUS" api POST /v1/changes/<id>/merge`, a pull request merge, any forge call that merges - when the review carries no `MEASURED:` mark with numbers, when it says `MEASURED: owed`, or when the pull request is titled `[needs lane]`: say which of these it is, so the caller has a lane measure the change first. A change merges without numbers only when its review says `MEASURED: not needed: <why>` or its issue carries the label `no-measurement`, which is a person's decision and not yours to make. A number the builder reports that you did not see in the change, a figure from another topology and a run of your own are not the measurement the item asks for. Do not weaken this rule and do not merge around it.

## ngram-ssd-only
On the Moebius host (this machine), Hy4-flash's Engram (n-gram) tables stay on the SSD and are never held in memory: every radiance instance a run starts here - serving, rad-kbench, a served A/B, a KL or end-to-end measurement - runs with `ngram-placement: disk`, or `disk=DIR` with `DIR` on the SSD for a table in its own file, and never with `ram`, `ram=DIR` or `auto`; no copy of the table is made, pinned or locked in this host's RAM, only the rows a kernel gathers pass through memory. The point is that a radiance instance cannot push this machine's memory into the OOM killer again. The rule is about what runs on this machine, not about the code: a change that adds or improves `ram`, `ram=DIR` or `auto` placement (such as B-02), a config for another machine, or a measurement a contributor took on their own machine with those placements is not refused for that reason and is reviewed on its merits.
reason: Person: the ngram-ssd-only rule applies only to this machine (too little RAM here), not to contributors' code or machines
